result.summary: This section gathers short ancient quotations and reports from Hesiod's lost 'Marriage of Ceyx'. They mention Heracles being left behind in Magnesia, his visits to Ceyx of Trachis, a proverb about good men at feasts, and a riddling description of firewood.

scenes.title: Heracles left behind in Magnesia
scenes.summary: A scholiast reports that Heracles landed from the Argo to find water and was left behind near Aphetae in Magnesia.
scenes.stakes: Heracles is separated from the Argo expedition.

scenes.title: Heracles at the house of Ceyx
scenes.summary: Heracles often visits Ceyx at Trachis and speaks a proverb about good men and feasts. A fragment mentions Ceyx as a horse-driver, and Athenaeus defends the poem's antiquity.

scenes.title: Wood brought for the fire
scenes.summary: After the feast, dry wood is brought from the forest to be burned, described in riddling language.

characters.name: Heracles
characters.description: hero who sailed on the Argo and visited Ceyx

notable_quotes.reason: Preserves a proverb: the good go of their own accord to the feasts of the good.

analysis.text: The fragments center on hospitality and feasting, with Heracles as a guest at Ceyx's house, and on the proverbial wisdom of the good.
The poem survives only in quotations by scholiasts and writers, and even in antiquity its Hesiodic authorship was disputed.

fun_facts.text: Athenaeus says schoolboys denied Hesiod wrote the poem, but he still thought it ancient.

language_notes.text: A scholiast is an ancient commentator whose marginal notes (scholia) on a text preserve fragments like this one.
The Argo was Jason's ship in the quest for the Golden Fleece. Heracles was said to be left behind during the voyage.
'Of their own selves the good make for the feasts of good' means good men come uninvited to the feasts of other good men.
'Grammar-school boys alienate it' means schoolmasters deny that Hesiod wrote it; Athenaeus disagrees, judging it ancient.
'Mother of a mother' is a riddling kenning for wood; the note explains it, and 'slain by her own children' means burnt by fire.
'Equal-shared feast' means a feast where everyone received a fair portion, a stock Homeric-style expression.

context_notes.text: Ceyx was king of Trachis in Thessaly, a friend and host of Heracles. Zenobius collected proverbs.
Athenaeus was a writer of the late second century AD whose Deipnosophistae preserves many fragments about dining.

literary_notes.text: 'Horse-driving' is a formulaic descriptive title attached to Ceyx, in the style of epic poetry.
Wood is called the mother of a mother, and its burning a killing by its own children, turning fire-making into a family tragedy.
